source.title: Recurrent Guillain-Barré Syndrome – Case Series
source.source_type: multicenter descriptive recurrent-GBS case series within a GBS cohort

atoms.canonical_statement: The study aimed to identify patients with previous GBS episodes and characterize recurrent GBS in a large cohort of adults with GBS.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the aim was to identify clinical features of RGBS in a large cohort of adult GBS patients.

atoms.canonical_statement: During a 6-year period, 404 patients with GBS were hospitalized at seven tertiary health care centers in Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina (Republic of Srpska), and Montenegro.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: During a 6-year period, 404 GBS patients were hospitalized in seven tertiary health care centers

population.label: GBS patients hospitalized at seven tertiary centers in three Balkan countries

atoms.canonical_statement: GBS was diagnosed when patients fulfilled standard National Institute of Neurological Diseases and Stroke criteria.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The diagnosis of GBS was made if patients fulfilled the standard National Institute of Neurological Diseases and Stroke (NINDS) criteria.

population.label: GBS cohort
inclusion_criteria: Fulfilled standard NINDS criteria for GBS

atoms.canonical_statement: GBS subtypes were assigned from clinical and electrophysiological findings.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A definitive diagnosis of GBS subtypes was made according to the clinical and electrophysiological findings.

atoms.canonical_statement: Age, sex, preceding factors, nadir and discharge disability, cerebrospinal fluid findings, and therapy were obtained from medical records for current and previous episodes.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Sociodemographic and clinical data ... were obtained from medical records for actual and previous episodes.

atoms.canonical_statement: Functional disability was graded with the GBS disability scale from 0 (no symptoms) to 6 (lethal outcome); scores greater than 3 were defined as severe disability.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The GDS ranges from 0 (no symptoms) to 6 (lethal outcome), where >3 was defined as a severe disability.

outcome.definition: Scale 0=no symptoms to 6=lethal outcome; >3 defined as severe disability

atoms.canonical_statement: Recurrent GBS was defined according to suggestions by Kuitwaard et al.; the article does not restate those criteria.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: RGBS was defined according to suggestions by Kuitwaard et al.

atoms.canonical_statement: The analysis used descriptive statistics including mean, standard deviation, median, minimum, and maximum.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: methods of descriptive statistics were used including mean, standard deviation, median, minimum and maximum.

atoms.canonical_statement: Of 404 patients with GBS, 20 had a prior acute polyradiculoneuritis episode; five were excluded after follow-up as acute-onset CIDP and two were excluded because of comorbidities, leaving 13 recurrent GBS cases.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The final number of 13 (3.2%) RGBS patients were included.

atoms.canonical_statement: Recurrent GBS was identified in 13 of 404 patients (3.2%).

concept.text: Observed GBS cohort during the 6-year study period

outcome.definition: Patients meeting the study definition of recurrent GBS

atoms.canonical_statement: The recurrent GBS subset comprised 10 men (76.9%) and 3 women (23.1%), and all 13 patients had exactly two GBS episodes.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: 10 were males (76.9%) and three were females (23.1%). All of them had two episodes of GBS.

atoms.canonical_statement: Mean age was 40.8 ± 22.5 years at the first episode and 53.6 ± 12.5 years at the recurrent episode.
The mean interval between first and recurrent GBS episodes was 12.9 ± 15.1 years.
A preceding event occurred a mean 10.0 ± 8.4 days before the first episode and 7.7 ± 4.3 days before recurrence; the source reports P > 0.05.

concept.text: Time from preceding event to GBS episode

atoms.canonical_statement: The same preceding event was reported before both attacks in 15.4% of recurrent GBS patients.

concept.text: Same preceding event before both GBS attacks

quantitative_result.original_result_text: In 15.4% of patients, the preceding event was the same

atoms.canonical_statement: AIDP was present in 76.9% of first episodes and 84.6% of recurrent episodes.

quantitative_result.effect_measure: proportion with AIDP in first episode (%)
quantitative_result.original_result_text: 76.9% at the first and 84.6% in the second episode

atoms.canonical_statement: During recurrence, 23.1% of patients had a different GBS variant than during the first attack and 76.9% had the same variant.

quantitative_result.effect_measure: proportion with different variant at recurrence (%)

atoms.canonical_statement: Mean CSF protein was 1.4 ± 0.6 g/L at the first attack and 1.7 ± 1.3 g/L at recurrence; the source reports P > 0.05.

quantitative_result.effect_measure: mean CSF protein at first episode (g/L)

atoms.canonical_statement: Mean CSF pleocytosis was 2.2 ± 2.2/mm³ at the first episode and 4.5 ± 7.6/mm³ at recurrence; the source reports P > 0.05.
None of the 13 recurrent GBS patients had an autoimmune disease as a comorbid disorder.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: None of our RGBS patients had an autoimmune disease as a comorbid disorder.

atoms.canonical_statement: Mean GDS at nadir was 4.0 ± 0.6 (median 4) at the first attack and 3.8 ± 1.2 (median 4) at recurrence; the source reports P > 0.05.

quantitative_result.effect_measure: mean nadir GDS at first episode

atoms.canonical_statement: Mean GDS at discharge was 2.9 ± 0.8 (median 3) after the first attack and 2.9 ± 0.9 (median 3) after recurrence; the source reports P > 0.05.

quantitative_result.effect_measure: mean discharge GDS at first episode

atoms.canonical_statement: Severe disability at nadir was reported in 84.6% of first attacks and 76.9% of recurrent attacks; the source reports P > 0.05.

quantitative_result.effect_measure: proportion severely disabled at nadir in first episode (%)

atoms.canonical_statement: Severe disability at discharge was reported in 23.1% of patients after both the first and recurrent attacks.

quantitative_result.effect_measure: proportion severely disabled at discharge in first episode (%)
quantitative_result.original_result_text: 23.1% of patients both at the first and second GBS attack

atoms.canonical_statement: IVIg was used in 38.5% of first attacks and 92.3% of recurrent attacks.

quantitative_result.effect_measure: proportion receiving IVIg during first episode (%)

atoms.canonical_statement: Therapeutic plasma exchange was used in 23.1% of first attacks and in none of the recurrent attacks.

quantitative_result.effect_measure: proportion receiving plasma exchange during first episode (%)
quantitative_result.original_result_text: 23.1% ... first attack and it was not administered during the second attack

atoms.canonical_statement: Table 1 reports patient-level features for all 26 episodes in the 13 recurrent GBS cases, including age, preceding event, GBS variant, GDS at nadir, therapy, discharge GDS, and interval between attacks.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Main features of all episodes in our patients with GBS (n=13)

atoms.canonical_statement: The cause of recurrent GBS remained uncertain in this cohort; different preceding events and different GBS variants could occur in the same patient.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The cause of recurrence is still uncertain

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors proposed that individual immunologic differences and genetic host factors could modulate antiganglioside antibody and molecular-mimicry mechanisms; this was a discussion hypothesis rather than a tested study result.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: could modulate the well-known antiganglioside antibodies and molecular mimicry mechanisms.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors suggested that similar or lower disability during recurrence might relate to more frequent IVIg/plasma-exchange therapy during recurrent episodes; this was not tested as a causal treatment effect.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: It is possible that our patients did not have more severe disability during the second GBS episode since they received IVIg/PLEx therapy more frequently

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that recurrent GBS occurred in about 3% of their GBS cohort, nearly one-quarter of recurrent cases changed variant at the second attack, disability was similar across attacks, and immunomodulatory therapy was used more often during recurrence.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Almost one-quarter ... different variant ... disability was similar ... immunomodulatory therapy was more frequently applied during RGBS.

atoms.canonical_statement: The article reported no financial support or sponsorship.
The authors reported no conflicts of interest.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: There are no conflicts of interest.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors reported obtaining appropriate patient consent forms for publication of clinical information.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The authors certify that they have obtained all appropriate patient consent forms.
